name: Anthracnose leaf spot
summary: A confirmed Cannabis anthracnose leaf-spot disease. Tan-centered lesions can crack or drop out into shot-hole symptoms and coalesce into necrotic blotches, but those features still overlap other leaf-spot diseases.
indicators: Light-green specks become round or angular spots with tan centers, darker brown margins, and yellow halos
Lesion centers may crack or drop out, producing shot-hole or frog-eye appearance
Coalescing lesions can form larger necrotic regions and marginal lesions can cause scorching, puckering, or twisting
exclusions: Sooty underside conidial masses support Pseudocercospora
Laboratory testing identifies another leaf-spot pathogen
Physical holes occur without surrounding lesion development or pathogen evidence

progression.description: Spots become tan-centered with darker margins and halos.
Centers can crack or drop out and lesions may coalesce into larger necrotic areas.

confirmation: Use culture plus morphology and molecular identification when assigning Colletotrichum fioriniae.
Do not use shot-hole appearance alone as confirmation.
immediateActions: Preserve representative lesions for diagnosis and isolate heavily affected propagation material.
correctivePlan: Use pathogen-confirmed sanitation and disease management appropriate to the production system.
prevention: Reduce carryover of diseased debris and avoid prolonged foliage wetness where practical.
warnings: Shot-hole and frog-eye lesions are not species-specific.
The first report does not establish nationwide prevalence or a universal symptom sequence.

sources.title: First Report of Anthracnose Leaf Spot Caused by Colletotrichum fioriniae on Hemp (Cannabis sativa)
supportedClaims: Hemp anthracnose lesions began as light-green specks and developed into 3 to 4 mm round or angular spots with tan centers, darker brown margins, and yellow halos; centers could crack or drop out and lesions could coalesce.
Colletotrichum fioriniae was identified by morphology and four gene sequences, and inoculation reproduced characteristic leaf spots while controls remained symptomless.
Shot-hole or frog-eye appearance is not species-specific and must be differentiated from other fungal and bacterial leaf spots.
